title: Core Advanced: a model card built from outside
subtitle: Apple's larger on-device model, measured on a MacBook Pro M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1

rows.text: Core Advanced, the larger on-device model of Apple's third generation
Apple, "custom-built in collaboration with Google"
The OS 27.0 model; no API to pin or read a version
Sparse decoder; experts chosen per prompt, built on Instruction-Following Pruning
20 billion stored, 1 to 4 billion active per request
56: the first 12 dense, which also compute the routing; 44 with experts
212 per expert layer, hidden size 256, plus always-active shared experts
Per prompt, reselected about every 32 tokens
Grouped-query; the cache fits 8 KV heads of 128 in 35 layers at 8 bits
rows.sub: the paper prints 12 query and KV heads, which the measured cache cannot fit

rows.text: 8,192 tokens
262,144 entries: Gemma 3's tokenizer, 775 reserved slots reused
Text and images in, text out; no reasoning mode
24 locales in the public API, 15 languages; it answered in all 10 test languages, Arabic, Hindi and Russian among them, outside the list
rows.sub: multilingual training; safety models loaded per language (Apple says, system log)

rows.text: About 2 bits per weight, quantization-aware training
rows.sub: Apple: 2 bits for the 2025 model, no bit width for 2026

rows.text: A 192 MiB table: 4 bits at width 1,536
8 bits; 35 MiB at a 512-token window, 560 MiB at 8,192
rows.sub: the sizes are measured; the 8 bits are inferred

rows.text: A 4.95 GB file in flash, read in 294,912-byte blocks
636 MiB of resident model pages; 2.0 to 3.4 GiB with the safety models
Neural Engine, about 4 W; GPU idle
Draft model for speculative decoding (about 9 MiB), use-case adapter, two 300M safety models
Public, licensed, open-source, study and synthetic data; no proportions
